name: Porsche
overview: The pre-eminent German sports car manufacturer, with Australia holding the distinction of being Porsche's very first right-hand-drive market in the world.
australian_history: Australia occupies a revered position in Porsche's global history. In 1951, Australian entrepreneur Norman Hamilton traveled to Gmünd and Stuttgart, meeting Ferry Porsche and securing the franchise to import the very first right-hand-drive Porsche 356 models in the world. The first two cars—a Fish Silver Grey 356 Coupe and Cabriolet—arrived in Melbourne in late 1951. Hamilton founded Porsche Cars Australia, operating out of South Melbourne. In 1992, Porsche AG acquired the distributorship directly. Australia became a stronghold for Porsche Carrera Cup racing and sports car sales, with the 911, Boxster, Cayman, Cayenne, Macan, and all-electric Taycan enjoying passionate support.

models.overview: The definitive rear-engine sports car. Australia boasts one of the most historic ties to Porsche in the world: Melbourne businessman Norman Hamilton secured the Australian concession in 1951, importing two 356s that represented the first right-hand drive Porsches ever made. Since the 911's local launch in 1965, it has defined sports car perfection through air-cooled and water-cooled eras, culminating in legendary Turbo, GT3, and GT3 RS icons.

911.overview: The definitive rear-engine sports car. Australia boasts one of the most historic ties to Porsche in the world: Melbourne businessman Norman Hamilton secured the Australian concession in 1951, importing two 356s that represented the first right-hand drive Porsches ever made. Since the 911's local launch in 1965, it has defined sports car perfection through air-cooled and water-cooled eras, culminating in legendary Turbo, GT3, and GT3 RS icons.
911.australian_market_notes: In late 1951, Norman Hamilton brought the first two RHD 356 coupes to Australia (chassis 10517 and 10518). In motorsport, Jim Richards won multiple Australian Targa and touring car events in 911s. Australia consistently registers one of the world's highest proportions of Porsche GT cars (GT3, GT3 RS, GT2 RS) per capita.

cayenne-macan.australian_market_notes: The Cayenne arrived in Australia in mid-2003 to initial skepticism that rapidly dissolved as buyers experienced its astonishing handling and 3,500kg towing prowess. In 2014, the Macan debuted, quickly capturing huge waiting lists in Sydney and Melbourne.
